overview: Real Chinese rover LIBS peak measurements and calibrated SWIR spectra from author-published open datasets. Exact target coordinates and a verified per-target major-oxide table are not bundled.

summary.count_note: Rows in different publications/tables may describe the same target; counts are not additive unique observations.

landing_context.latitude_convention: not specified in cited coordinate statement
landing_context.note: Rounded published landing-site coordinates; not the position of any LIBS or SWIR target. Do not place the unlocated measurements here.

instrument_scope: MarSCoDe combines LIBS, short-wave infrared spectroscopy and a microimaging camera. Its SWIR mineralogy data are a different measurement from Raman; no Chinese Mars Raman dataset is included.

access.title: Imported open data
access.description: Five author-published LIBS spreadsheets and a calibrated SWIR archive were downloaded from Zenodo; original files, checksum verification and source rows are bundled.

access.title: Primary Level 2B LIBS spectra
access.description: Luo et al. state that CLPDS data are open after registration. No account-restricted primary spectra were downloaded for this version.

access.title: Major-oxide and trace-concentration supplement
access.description: Luo et al. Table S2 is listed by the publisher, but its public download returned HTTP 403 during this build. Peak ratios have not been converted to concentrations.

interpretations.title: Gypsum-rich platy rocks
interpretations.summary: Liu et al. (2026) interpret platy rocks as a primary gypsum/selenite evaporite using crystal morphology, infrared absorptions and LIBS sulfur, hydrogen and calcium. This is mineralogical context, not an organic detection.

interpretations.title: Weathering rinds
interpretations.summary: Zhang et al. (2025) interpret spectra of some dark rock patches as consistent with silica-enriched leached rinds on basaltic glass. Dust cover and mixed fields of view affect interpretation.

notes: Normalized LIBS peak area is a signal ratio, not elemental or oxide concentration. Numeric scales vary by line and processing method.
Hydrogen, sulfur or chlorine peaks alone do not demonstrate organic molecules, habitability or life.
Target labels and sol numbers are preserved. Different paper naming conventions have not been joined without an explicit identifier crosswalk.
No continuous compositional field, organic region or exact target geography is inferred from these data.

sources.title: Luo et al. (2024), Alkali trace elements observed by MarSCoDe LIBS
Zhang et al. (2024), Volatile elements characterized by MarSCoDe

peak_tables.title: Li and major-element peak areas
peak_tables.notes: Published normalized LIBS peak areas; these are not concentrations, wt% or mineral abundances. The paper normalizes spectra by the integrated intensity of each instrument channel; Li uses VNIR and Sr uses VIS. The original Mg 518.51 column label is retained, although repository metadata says 518.15 nm.

peak_tables.title: Sr and major-element peak areas
peak_tables.notes: Published normalized LIBS peak areas; these are not concentrations, wt% or mineral abundances. The paper normalizes spectra by the integrated intensity of each instrument channel; Li uses VNIR and Sr uses VIS. The original Mg 518.51 column label is retained, although repository metadata says 518.15 nm.

peak_tables.title: S and major-element peak areas
peak_tables.notes: Published normalized LIBS peak areas; these are not concentrations, wt% or mineral abundances. The paper describes S 564 nm normalization to O 777 nm; do not compare its numeric scale with the Li/Sr tables.

peak_tables.title: H, S and Cl fitted peaks
peak_tables.notes: Original fitted peak areas, goodness of fit, widths and normalized peak areas. Blank/dash cells mean not reported, not zero. H, S or Cl emission does not establish organic matter.

peak_tables.title: Major-element peaks in sulfur-bearing rocks
peak_tables.notes: Published normalized LIBS peak areas; these are not concentrations, wt% or mineral abundances.

swir.processing: The present SWIR reflectance spectra are calibrated with the white calibration target and smoothed by the despike and wavelet denoising filter.
swir.note: These are short-wave infrared reflectance spectra, not Raman spectra. Mineral identifications require band analysis and reference spectra; the app does not automatically identify a mineral from a trough.
